items.t: **WARROOM 1.1** — MCDP-CODEX.html at root, built by _tools/mcdp_codex_build.py from its template; the eleven MIL one-sheets browsable on the [[ck3-rules|CK3 rules]] (concept links, nested tooltips depth 3, timer or key lock).

**The [[watch-register|WATCH register]]** (working name) — one grammar, two faces keyed to room light: DAY positive-polarity for the lit desk, NIGHT near-black for the light off; seven hues, contrast-checked; type in the 16 to 22 arcmin window; a three-step contrast control. Spec in _0.1_BVX_LEARN/_meta/WATCH-REGISTER.md.

**The finding that reshaped it:** no standard prefers dark themes for comfort; polarity is keyed to ambient light (MIL-STD-1472H 5.2.2.6; FAA HF-STD-001B 5.3.2.1.6). Your room is lit, so DAY is the working face. Research banked in LONG-WATCH-STANDARDS.md.
Three rulings on the card (filing · name · DARKROOM), plus the retint question raised by the 9/10 colorway ruling: the pages went orange; WARROOM still wears WATCH.

**1.1 on the WATCH register** — DAY and NIGHT faces.

**Live in it** with the light on and off. Standing note from the spec: face the monitor, keep the wall behind it within a third to three times the screen luminance, monitor white about 100 to 150 cd/m² lit, dim before warm.
**Rule the three** — filing · name · DARKROOM. Each is one line or one token swap.
**The retint question** — orange (the 9/10 default) or exempt.
